text.en: When using `/video-recap` to process a local video I provide, I will specify whether I want an original-audio short or a narrated recap and identify dialogue, actions, and reactions that must remain. This starts the video-understanding and production workflow. If I only want to discuss cut points, I will state that this round should provide revision advice only, without editing, voice-over, or rendering. In Codex, use `$video-recap`.

title.zh: 小说转场怎么写：让前一场把读者送进下一场
title.en: How to Write Scene Transitions: Let One Scene Lead into the Next

seo_title.zh: 小说转场怎么写｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Write Scene Transitions in Fiction | ZenStory

description.zh: 小说场景切换不必交代全部路程。判断何时跳切，再用未完成的因果、问题、情绪余波或物件声音承接下一场。附原创气象站案例。
description.en: Decide when to jump ahead, then bridge scenes through causality, questions, emotional residue, objects, or sound. Includes a weather-station example.

answer.zh: 自然转场要让前一场留下能跨过切口的东西：下一步行动、待回答的问题、尚未消化的情绪，或会在新地点继续出现的物件与声音。一句“与此同时”和完整赶路都不是必需。没有值得展开作用的过程可以直接跳过；新场开头要尽快说明谁、在哪里、正在处理什么，按这场的阅读作用继续承接。
answer.en: A natural transition carries something across the cut: the next action, an unanswered question, an unprocessed emotion, or an object or sound that continues in the new place. Neither “meanwhile” nor a complete travel sequence is required. Skip processes that serve no intended purpose. At the start of the new scene, quickly establish who is present, where they are, and what they are handling, and continue according to this scene’s intended effect.

heading.zh: 先判断：这一段需要写，还是应该跳过
heading.en: First Decide: Does This Passage Need a Scene, or Should You Skip It?

body.zh:
场景结束后，列出人物抵达下一场之前可能发生的步骤。根据本书重心，优先保留信息、关系、风险、资源、选择或情绪值得展开的步骤；买票、乘车、开门若只是完成移动，可以一句带过或直接切到结果。

转场不是独立的填充段。它至少完成一项工作：兑现上一场的后果、提出下一步目标、保存一股情绪压力，或把读者注意力交给另一条线。删掉切口附近的句子再读，若人物为何来到新场仍然清楚，就不必把路程补回来。
body.en:
After a scene ends, list the steps that might occur before the character reaches the next one. Prioritize steps whose information, relationships, risk, resources, choices or emotion deserve attention in this book. Buying a ticket, riding a train, or opening a door can be summarized in one line or skipped if it only completes movement.

A transition is not an independent filler passage. It must do at least one job: deliver the consequence of the last scene, establish the next goal, preserve emotional pressure, or hand the reader’s attention to another plotline. Remove the sentences around the cut and reread. If it remains clear why the character has arrived in the new scene, you do not need to restore the journey.

heading.zh: 四种可跨场的承接物
heading.en: Four Things That Can Bridge Scenes

body.zh:
| 承接方式 | 前后场的联系 |
|---|---|
| 因果 | 前一场留下什么：一个决定、命令或损失；新一场怎样接：直接写它造成的下一步行动 |
| 问题 | 前一场留下什么：一个具体未解疑问；新一场怎样接：用调查、误判或局部答案推进 |
| 情绪余波 | 前一场留下什么：人物尚未处理的羞愧、兴奋或戒备；新一场怎样接：让它改变新场中的说法与选择 |
| 物件或声音 | 前一场留下什么：信件、污迹、铃声、广播等具体对象；新一场怎样接：在新时空获得新用途或含义 |

同一处选最有力的一条即可。相似物、光影或声音可以让画面顺滑，其价值也可以是对照、氛围或停留，不要求新场立即得到线索；同时检查人物与时间是否让读者误读。反过来，只要因果清楚，干净的空行也可以完成跳切。

Oh Story 的 style-craft 提供相似物、感知和情绪的衔接法；style-resolution 让具体写法服从作者和本书文风。上表是编辑比较卡，不是原生章节格式。因果桥、干净跳切和安静停留可以按本次需要组合，不机械要求四种桥都用一遍。
body.en:
| Bridge | Scene connection |
|---|---|
| Causality | Before: A decision, order, or loss; After: Show the next action it directly causes |
| Question | Before: One specific unresolved question; After: Advance it through investigation, misjudgment, or a partial answer |
| Emotional residue | Before: Shame, excitement, or wariness the character has not processed; After: Let it alter what the character says and chooses in the new scene |
| Object or sound | Before: A concrete item such as a letter, stain, bell, or broadcast; After: Give it a new use or meaning in the new time and place |

Choose the strongest one at a given cut. Similar objects, light, or sound can smooth the image, and can provide contrast, atmosphere, or a pause without an immediate clue. Still check whether readers can place the characters and time. Conversely, when causality is clear, a clean section break can complete the jump.

Oh Story’s style-craft offers object, perception, and emotional links; style-resolution places the author’s and book’s choices first. This is an editorial comparison, not the native chapter format. Combine a causal bridge, clean cut, or quiet pause as needed rather than cycling through every method.

heading.zh: 新场开头先给定位，再制造变化
heading.en: Orient the Reader at the New Scene, Then Create Change

body.zh:
新场第一小段回答读者此刻真正需要的三件事：视角人物是谁、地点或时间发生了什么变化、他正处理上一场留下的哪件事。不要把日期、天气、房间陈设和人物履历一次性重报。

承接不等于复述。上一场以“她决定去查停机记录”结束，新场无需再写“她想着一定要查清”。让她已经站在档案柜前，却发现要找的一页不在册中，读者会从行动认出承接，同时收到新变化。多线切换时，可让各线切出前留下目标、情绪或未解问题，切回时承接已有状态。群像或日常作品也可以回到关系与生活，不必每条线都像调查一样追问答案。

“缺页”是眼前可见的状态，“有人替换”是需要对照或其他依据的判断；若下一步要查替换者，先让调查取得支持，不用一个转场直接送出幕后答案。
body.en:
The first short passage of a new scene should answer the three things readers actually need now: whose viewpoint this is, what has changed in time or place, and which matter from the prior scene the character is addressing. Do not report the date, weather, room furnishings, and character history all over again.

A bridge is not a recap. If the prior scene ends with “She decided to inspect the shutdown records,” the new scene need not repeat that she was determined to investigate. Put her at the archive cabinet, where the page she needs is absent. Readers recognize the continuation through action and receive a new change at the same time. When alternating plotlines, a line can leave a goal, emotion, or unresolved question and return with its established state intact. An ensemble or slice-of-life story can revisit relationships and ordinary life without making every line pursue an investigative answer.

An absent page is visible; replacement by someone requires comparison or other support. If the next step concerns who replaced it, let the investigation establish a basis rather than having the transition supply the hidden answer.

heading.zh: 原创范例：山顶气象站的两次切换
heading.en: Original Example: Two Transitions at a Mountaintop Weather Station

body.zh:
实习观测员简遥发现自动雨量记录与手写值不同。值班长允许她先核对耗材批号和原记录；原因尚未确定。记录纸包装标着一种旧纸卷型号，本站登记写有镇上供应店。她决定去库房找同型号余卷作对照。

**拖沓版**逐步写收本子、穿衣、下楼、走廊、开锁，途中没有新作用。

**因果跳切**：

> 库房那层货架空了。简遥翻开余料登记，最后一卷已领走；她把日期和型号记在笔记里，给镇店打了电话。

空货架回答“这里有没有余卷”，登记给出一个已知领取日期，不证明纸卷有问题或有人篡改雨量。镇店答应次日开门后查旧进货记录，她便按约去。

**第二次切换**：

> 次日九点，供应店的卷帘门升起来。老板把旧单据推到柜台上：“这个型号三年前停止进货。你要找余卷，先看以前那批客户。”

时间、地点与目标同时清楚，电话约定被兑现。单据缩小采购方向，没有据此断定观测数据造假；简遥下一步核对其他采购渠道和纸卷适配信息。

赶路可以跳过，若路上本来包含新选择则照常写。转场以清楚承接为准，安静的新场也可以先停留，不必每次立刻出事故。
body.en:
Trainee observer Jian Yao finds automatic rainfall records differ from handwritten values. The supervisor permits checking supplies and original records; cause remains unknown. Packaging names an old paper-roll model, and the station’s supplier entry identifies a town shop. Jian wants a spare roll for comparison.

**Dragging version:** packing notes, putting on a coat, walking downstairs and opening the store room, with no new function.

**Causal cut:**

> The shelf was empty. The supplies register showed the last roll taken out. Jian noted the date and model and called the town shop.

The shelf answers whether a spare exists; the entry gives a withdrawal date without proving a defective roll or altered rainfall. The shop agrees to check old purchasing records when it opens next morning.

**Second cut:**

> At nine the next day, the shutter rose. The owner pushed old invoices across the counter. “We stopped buying this model three years ago. Check that batch’s old customers for spares.”

Time, place and aim are clear, and the appointment is fulfilled. The invoice narrows supply inquiries without proving forged readings. Jian next checks other purchasing channels and roll compatibility.

Skip travel unless it contains a relevant choice. Clear continuation matters; a quiet new scene can linger without an instant accident.

heading.zh: 转场生硬或拖沓时怎么改
heading.en: How to Repair Abrupt or Dragging Transitions

body.zh:
| 症状：原因 | 修正 |
| --- | --- |
| 每次都写人物离开、赶路、抵达：把空间连续误当成叙事连续 | 跳到下一次有变化的动作 |
| 切到新人物后读者不知为何：只用“与此同时”代替定位和联系 | 补必要定位；联系可以来自共同事件、对照、情绪或本书群像安排 |
| 新场开头复述上一场结论：只承接，没有推进 | 从结论造成的阻碍、发现或选择写起 |
| 用相似物硬转，逻辑却断了：视觉相似代替了因果 | 补清谁为何来到这里、要处理什么 |
| 高压场后立刻完全松弛：情绪结果被清零 | 让余波改变新场的节奏或人物策略 |
| 频繁切线却迟迟不回来：每条线只留钩子不交付 | 切回时先回答一部分，再提出新问题 |
body.en:
| Problem and cause | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Every scene shows the character leaving, traveling, and arriving: Spatial continuity is mistaken for narrative continuity | Jump to the next action that changes something |
| Readers cannot place a cut to another person: “Meanwhile” substitutes for orientation and connection | Supply necessary orientation; shared events, contrast, emotion, or the work’s ensemble design can provide the link |
| A new scene opens by repeating the last scene’s conclusion: The transition continues but does not advance | Begin with the obstacle, discovery, or choice caused by that conclusion |
| A similar image forces a transition while the logic breaks: Image matching has replaced cause | Clarify who came here, why, and what they need to handle |
| A tense scene cuts away with its effects forgotten: The emotional consequence has been reset | Carry its effects into the next scene; earned relief can be a response |
| The narrative switches lines repeatedly and takes too long to return: Every line leaves hooks but delivers nothing | On returning, answer something before raising a new question |

q.zh: 转场一定要写过渡句吗？
q.en: Does every scene transition need a transitional sentence?

a.zh: 不需要。因果清楚时，分段、空行或新章节就能完成转场。过渡句只在时间、地点或人物关系容易误读时补足必要定位。
a.en: No. When causality is clear, a section break, blank line, or new chapter can complete the transition. Add a transitional sentence only when time, location, or relationships would otherwise be misread.

q.zh: 同一章可以切换很多场景吗？
q.en: Can one chapter contain many scene changes?

a.zh: 可以。让读者迅速定位，并检查切换服务的是信息、行动、情绪、对照还是陪伴。没有必要每次都增加事件；几个短场若只是无作用地重复结论，再合并或保留更有效的一场。
a.en: Yes. Reorient readers and check whether the switch serves information, action, emotion, contrast, or companionship. Every cut need not add an event. Combine short scenes when they merely repeat a conclusion without a useful effect.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 检查这几处场景转场，逐处判断哪些过程应跳过，并标出跨场的因果、问题、情绪余波或物件声音；让新场开头快速定位并推进，不改既有剧情事实”（Codex 中使用 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/story-long-write` to inspect these scene transitions. At each one, decide which process should be skipped and identify the causality, question, emotional residue, object, or sound that crosses the cut. Orient the reader quickly at each new scene and move it forward without changing established plot facts.” In Codex, use `$story-long-write`.

label.zh: 相似物、感知与情绪承接

title.zh: 小说回忆怎么写：让过去改变眼前的选择
title.en: How to Write Flashbacks: Make the Past Change a Present Choice

seo_title.zh: 小说回忆与插叙怎么写不打断剧情｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Write Flashbacks Without Stalling | ZenStory

description.zh: 回忆和插叙要由当前场景触发，只带回会改变判断、关系或选择的过去事实，并在返回当下后产生动作。附原创修琴案例。
description.en: Trigger a flashback from the present, retrieve only what changes judgment, relationships, or choice, then act on it. Includes a repair-shop example.

answer.zh: 写回忆先确定它怎样改变读者对现在的理解。用眼前物件、声音、话语或处境接回过去，再按本书叙述方式控制时段与返回位置。回忆可以影响行动，也可以深化关系和情绪；已有片段原样重复而无新作用时，压缩或换一个真正不同的观察。
answer.en: Decide how a flashback changes understanding of the present. Connect past and present through an object, sound, remark or situation, then control its period and return in the book’s narrative style. It can change action or deepen relationships and emotion. Compress a repeated scene when it adds no new function.

heading.zh: 先写回忆带回来的新作用
heading.en: First Define the New Function the Flashback Brings Back

body.zh:
先问回忆给当前阅读带来什么：信息、关系理解、情绪，还是一个决定。它可以让人物行动，也可以让读者重新理解一句沉默，不必每段都产生新动作。

| 带回什么 | 可以怎样使用 |
|---|---|
| 被忽略的事实 | 重新检查怀疑对象或行动方向 |
| 旧承诺 | 重新理解当前的请求或拒绝 |
| 某人的一贯做法 | 形成预判，随后由现实验证 |
| 关系中的误读 | 改变读者对疏远、亲近或遗憾的理解 |

只有人物档案式背景时，可以概述；想让读者亲历过去的关系、情绪或转折时，可以展开。篇幅取决于本书重心，而不是“有回忆就必须推动新事件”。

先分清两种写法：人物回忆只含他当时经历过、后来确实获知或如今能够想起的内容；叙述者切到过去的插叙则按本书视角展开。读者看见一段过去，不代表当前人物也因此知道其中全部事实。以下连接表是编辑用的检查方法，不是原生文件模板。
body.en:
Ask what a flashback adds to the present reading: information, a relationship, emotion or a decision. It can prompt action or let readers understand a silence differently; every memory need not produce a new act.

| What returns | Possible use |
|---|---|
| Overlooked fact | Recheck a suspect or direction |
| Old promise | Reinterpret a present request or refusal |
| Habitual conduct | Form an expectation for reality to test |
| Misread relationship | Change readers’ understanding of distance, closeness or regret |

Dossier-like background may be summarized. Expand when readers should experience a past relationship, emotion or turn. Length follows the book’s focus, rather than a demand that every memory start a new event.

Distinguish a character’s memory from a narrator’s move into an earlier period. Memory stays within what the character experienced, actually learned later, or can now recall; a narrated past scene follows the book’s viewpoint. Readers seeing that scene does not give every present character its facts. The connection checklist is an editorial aid, not a native file template.

heading.zh: 用当前触发进入，用当前动作退出
heading.en: Enter Through a Present Trigger and Exit Through Present Action

body.zh:
行动型回忆可以用三个连接点：当前触发、过去的关键片段、回到当前后的响应。摸到琴箱裂口，想起上次修补，回来时仍握着裂口，再决定是否交琴。

写情绪或关系时，响应也可以是对同一物件的新感受，或者读者对人物沉默的新理解。触发不必明说“陷入回忆”；明确的时间标记、段落分隔也能带入过去。返回时给一个当前的位置、对象或声音，让读者辨认时空。
body.en:
For an action-focused memory, try three links: a present trigger, a relevant past scene and a response on return. Touching an instrument case’s crack recalls its repair; the character returns still holding it and decides whether to hand over the instrument.

For emotion or relationships, the response may be a changed feeling toward the same object, or the reader’s new understanding of a silence. A flashback need not announce itself: a time marker or section break can introduce the past. On return, supply a current place, object or sound to orient readers.

heading.zh: 回忆写到哪里停：以当前问题为边界
heading.en: Where to End a Flashback: Let the Present Question Set the Boundary

body.zh:
从当前要给读者的新理解决定范围。此刻只需知道师父为何拆扣，就不用顺带补童年、搬家与求学；但过去自身的冲突值得亲历时，可以展开。长度由作用和本书文风决定，不固定句数。

较长回忆要让读者清楚过去的时段与现在的未结事，返回时补足定位。它可以形成对照、情绪停留或关系理解，不必每次立即变成一个新决定；真正要删的是无新作用的重复。
body.en:
Let the new understanding determine scope. If readers only need why the mentor removed the clasp, do not add childhood, moves and schooling. Expand when the past’s own conflict matters. Use function and book style, not a sentence quota.

For a long flashback, distinguish its time from the open present situation and reorient on return. Contrast, emotional reflection and relationship understanding can matter without an immediate new decision. Cut repetition that adds no function.

heading.zh: 原创范例：琴箱里少了一枚铜扣
heading.en: Original Example: A Missing Brass Clasp in the Instrument Case

body.zh:
古琴修复师许潭筠准备把自己所有的琴和琴箱捐给博物馆。验收员发现右侧铜扣缺失，问是否运输中损坏；尚未填写责任结论。许潭筠本以为自己漏查，摸到扣眼里一层旧蜡，想起一件事。

十二岁那年停电，师父在烛下拆下铜扣，用它垫住摇晃的工作台。她问为何不找木片，师父说次日要修受损的琴，今晚先把桌子稳住。蜡滴到了扣眼；铜扣后来未装回，她当时只觉得师父粗心。

回到验收室，她说明自己记得拆扣，提议先核对出运前照片，而不是立即签“运输损坏”。验收员实际暂停这个栏目的签认，两人调出装箱记录：出运照片已经显示缺扣。这支持缺扣先于本次运输，不替两人证明全部旧蜡年代或琴的完整来历。

许潭筠后来还想把工作台一起捐出。桌子仍在她所有的铺里，她补交物件说明和捐赠申请；博物馆是否接收须另作评估，本场没有把“列清单”写成已经入藏。

过去让她重新理解师父的取舍，也让眼前处理从自责转为核对记录。若读者已见过完整拆扣场景，压成“他拿这枚扣垫过桌脚”，再写当前请求即可，不原样重播。
body.en:
Instrument restorer Xu Tanyun plans to donate a zither and its case, both hers, to a museum. An inspector notices the missing right brass clasp and asks about transport damage; no responsibility finding has been entered. Xu fears she missed it, then touches old wax in the hole and remembers.

At twelve, during a blackout, she watched her mentor remove the clasp and steady a wobbling worktable with it. He wanted the table ready to repair a damaged instrument the next morning. Wax dripped into the clasp hole. The clasp never returned; she had dismissed it as carelessness.

Back at inspection, Xu describes the removal and asks to compare pre-shipment photographs before signing “transport damage.” The inspector actually pauses that field. The packing record shows the clasp missing before departure. This supports prior absence, not a precise wax date or the complete provenance of the instrument.

Xu also wants to donate the table, still hers at the workshop. She submits its description and a separate donation request. Museum acceptance needs further assessment; listing it is not accession.

The past changes her understanding of the mentor’s tradeoff and turns self-blame into a record check. If readers already saw the removal, compress it to a reminder and the present request rather than replay it.

heading.zh: 回忆打断剧情的常见原因
heading.en: Why Flashbacks Commonly Interrupt the Plot

body.zh:
| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 角色一见物件就回顾完整人生 | 按本场需要的信息、关系或情绪取舍，不顺带复述无关前史 |
| 回忆重复读者刚看过的事件 | 增加新的视角或压成一句承接 |
| 回忆很长，却未增加对当前的理解或体验 | 先检查关系、情绪、判断与行动的作用；没有才删减或换位置 |
| 回忆中继续套回忆 | 选一个明确时段，其他信息概述 |
| 用大段前史解释世界规则 | 把当前规则放回行动后果，回忆只留人物经验 |
| 回到现在没有定位 | 重现触发物、未完动作或正在等待的对方 |

修订时把“进入前的当前问题”和“返回后的新动作”并排看。若没有新动作，再检查它是否改变理解、情绪或关系。几项都没有，才考虑删减或换位置。
body.en:
| Failure | Fix |
|---|---|
| A character sees an object and reviews an entire life | Select for this passage’s information, relationship, or emotion instead of reciting unrelated history |
| The flashback repeats an event readers just witnessed | Add a new viewpoint or compress it to one bridging sentence |
| A long flashback adds no understanding or experience of the present | Check its effect on relationships, emotion, judgment, and action; trim or move it when none matters |
| One flashback nests another | Choose one clear period and summarize the rest |
| A long backstory explains all the world’s rules | Put current rules back into the consequences of action; keep only lived experience in the memory |
| The return to the present has no orientation | Reintroduce the trigger, unfinished action, or waiting person |

During revision, place the present question before the flashback beside the new action after it. If there is no new action, check for a changed understanding, emotion or relationship. If none appears, consider trimming or moving it.

q.zh: 回忆可以放在小说开头吗？
q.en: Can a novel open with a flashback?

a.zh: 可以。若是人物正在回想，给出足够的身份、时段与返回定位；不必先制造危机。若开头整段就在过去，直接从那个时段开始也可以。后文再接现在时，写清时间变化即可，不必硬标“回忆”。
a.en: Yes. If a character is remembering, supply enough identity, timing, and orientation on return without inventing a crisis. If the opening simply takes place in the past, begin directly in that period. Clearly mark the later move to the present rather than forcing a memory label.

q.zh: 怎样区分回忆和设定介绍？
q.en: How is a flashback different from worldbuilding exposition?

a.zh: 人物回忆重现其经历或确实获知的过去，叙述者插叙则按本书视角进入过去时段；设定介绍说明世界如何运作。它们可以相遇，但不要借一次回忆讲完所有规则，也不要把读者得知写成人物已经知道。
a.en: A character’s memory recalls lived or actually learned history; a narrated flashback enters an earlier period in the book’s viewpoint. Exposition explains how the world works. They may overlap, but one memory need not explain every rule, and reader knowledge is not automatically character knowledge.

text.zh: 用 /story-long-write（Codex 用 $story-long-write）局部检查这段回忆或插叙，附前后文、本书视角与需保留的经历。先指出它对信息、关系、情绪或行动的作用，再检查进入过去和返回当前是否清楚。只删无作用的重复；不为满足模板新增经历或强造新动作。
text.en: Use /story-long-write, or $story-long-write in Codex, to inspect this flashback locally with surrounding prose, narrative viewpoint, and history to preserve. Identify its effect on information, relationships, emotion, or action, then check orientation into the past and back. Cut repetition without function; invent no history or action to fill a template.

label.zh: 回忆触发、篇幅与反注水
label.en: Memory triggers, scope, and avoiding filler

title.zh: 小说环境描写怎么写：让人物在场景里行动
title.en: How to Write Setting Description: Let Characters Act in the Scene

seo_title.zh: 小说环境描写怎么写才不水｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Writing Setting Description Without Padding | ZenStory

description.zh: 环境描写不靠景物清单，而要选择人物此刻会注意、会碰到、会因此改变行动的细节。附原创停电温室案例与删改方法。
description.en: Choose setting details a character would notice, touch, and act on instead of listing scenery. Includes a greenhouse blackout and revision method.

answer.zh: 先写人物进入场景要做什么，再选择会帮助、阻碍、误导或逼迫他的环境细节。描写落到主动注意、身体或工具与环境的交互，以及交互造成的判断和行动后果。气氛可以保留，但要通过具体感受影响阅读节奏；若删掉一段景物后人物处境、信息和体验都不变，就应压缩。
answer.en: Start with what the character must accomplish in the scene, then choose environmental details that help, obstruct, mislead, or pressure them. Description becomes part of the scene when it shows active attention, the body or a tool interacting with the surroundings, and the consequences for judgment and action. Atmosphere still matters, but it should shape reading rhythm through concrete sensation. If removing a passage leaves the character’s situation, information, and experience unchanged, compress it.

heading.zh: 按人物目标筛选环境信息
heading.en: Filter Setting Details Through the Character’s Goal

body.zh:
同一间仓库，失火后来找出口的人会注意风向、烟层与门把温度；来盘点货物的人会看标签、受潮痕迹与堆放顺序。环境细节由目标、经验和风险筛选，因而也能表现人物。

动笔前回答：人物来这里要完成什么？哪项环境条件会改变完成方式？他凭什么注意到这项条件？这样写出的景物属于当前场景，从而避免写成可搬到任何章节的装饰。
body.en:
In the same warehouse, a person searching for an exit after a fire notices wind direction, the smoke layer, and the temperature of a door handle. Someone taking inventory notices labels, damp marks, and stacking order. Goals, experience, and risk filter environmental details, so those details can also reveal character.

Before drafting, ask: What must the character accomplish here? Which environmental condition changes how it can be done? What qualifies the character to notice that condition? The resulting description belongs to this scene rather than serving as decoration that could be moved into any chapter.

heading.zh: 把景物写进“注意—交互—后果”
heading.en: Build Description as Attention, Interaction, and Consequence

body.zh:
| 环节 | 检查 |
|---|---|
| 注意 | **要写什么**：人物因目标、经验或此刻心情注意到的细节；**避免什么**：从天花板到地板逐项扫描 |
| 交互 | **要写什么**：触碰、绕开、借用、试探或被环境限制；**避免什么**：与本场目标无关的景物清单 |
| 后果 | **要写什么**：信息、行动、关系、身体状态或读者体验受到影响；**避免什么**：描写完立即忘记场景条件 |

五感不是配额。人物要通过湿滑地面时，触感可能比补齐颜色、气味、声音更重要；人物只是停留感受时，取舍也可以围绕气氛。动态变化尤其有效：光线熄灭、风把门推回、地面积水上涨，都能迫使人物重新选择。
body.en:
| Stage | Check |
|---|---|
| Attention | **What to write:** A detail the character notices because of a goal, experience, or present mood. **What to avoid:** Scanning item by item from ceiling to floor |
| Interaction | **What to write:** Touching, avoiding, using, testing, or being constrained by the environment. **What to avoid:** A scenery inventory unrelated to the reading goal |
| Consequence | **What to write:** An effect on information, action, relationships, physical state, or reader experience. **What to avoid:** Forgetting the conditions immediately after describing them |

The five senses are not a quota. For someone crossing a slippery floor, touch may matter more than filling in color, smell and sound. For someone pausing to experience a place, atmosphere can guide the selection instead. Dynamic changes are especially effective: the lights go out, wind pushes a door closed, or rising water forces the character to choose again.

heading.zh: 写气氛时，让场景产生压力而非替人物下结论
heading.en: For Atmosphere, Let the Setting Apply Pressure Instead of Declaring Emotion

body.zh:
“夜色压抑”“房间温馨”先给结论，读者却不知道这股气氛怎样发生。可以选择一两个会持续影响现场的条件：过亮的走廊让人无处躲藏；持续滴水让谈话一次次被打断；拥挤的桌椅迫使两人无法保持距离。

环境可以呼应情绪，也可以反衬。人物收到坏消息时窗外不必下雨；晴天里照常进行的庆典，反而可能加重他的孤立。关键是人物如何使用、抵抗或误读这个环境，天气无需替他感受。
body.en:
“The night felt oppressive” and “the room was cozy” announce conclusions without showing how the atmosphere occurs. Instead, choose one or two conditions that keep affecting the scene: an overlit corridor leaves nowhere to hide; steady dripping repeatedly interrupts a conversation; crowded furniture prevents two people from keeping their distance.

The setting may echo emotion or work against it. Bad news does not require rain outside. A celebration proceeding under bright skies can deepen a character’s isolation. What matters is how the character uses, resists, or misreads the setting. The weather need not feel on the character’s behalf.

heading.zh: 原创范例：停电后的社区温室
heading.en: Original Example: A Community Greenhouse After a Blackout

body.zh:
下面是为本页设计的虚构场景，展示空间条件怎样改变行动，不是温室养护建议。志愿者高槐音和邻居沈桐一同到社区温室，把靠门的三盘幼苗搬到已经获准借用的隔壁活动室。温室停电，浇水软管横在门槛上，门关不拢；两人各带一盏手电。

只写“温室又冷又黑”有气氛，却没说明人物怎样完成搬运。可以这样写：

> 高槐音把手电放到门边架子上，光只照到最外面的两盘。第三盘藏在架后，她侧过身，才看清盘底已经探出架沿。

> “你先抱这两盘。”她对沈桐说。沈桐先把自己的手电也放在架子上，再一手托一盘，绕过门槛上的软管往活动室走。

> 高槐音没去拉门，先把软管挪到门内，给回来的路腾出地方。她托住第三盘的底部，抱着它走到门外，再侧过身用肩膀把向外开启的门推回门框，门这才合上。两盏手电留在架子上，仍亮着，等沈桐回来取。

**条件与结果**：光照范围使第三盘需要另找角度；软管影响通行和关门，先挪开才有合门条件；沈桐的协助在开场已经建立。借用活动室已经获准，搬过去不等于幼苗得到长期安置。稿件若需要更多安全或园艺细节，另行查证，不从这个例子推导。

气味、温度或一段静景也能建立气氛和人物体验，不必每个细节都触发新事件。选择要服务本场阅读目标，而不是凑齐五感。
body.en:
This fictional scene demonstrates spatial cause and effect, rather than greenhouse care. Gao Huaiyin and neighbor Shen Tong arrive together to move three trays near the door to a neighboring activity room they already have permission to use. The greenhouse has lost power, a hose crosses the threshold and prevents the door from closing, and each person carries a torch.

“The greenhouse was cold and dark” supplies atmosphere without explaining the task. A scene could read:

> Gao Huaiyin set her torch on the shelf beside the door. Its beam reached only the outer two trays. The third was behind the rack; she turned sideways and saw its base projecting beyond the shelf.

> “Take these two first,” she told Shen Tong. Shen set his own torch on the shelf too, then supported one tray in each hand, stepped around the hose and headed to the activity room.

> She left the door alone and moved the hose inside, clearing their return path. She supported the third tray from beneath and carried it outside, then turned sideways and pushed the outward-opening door back into its frame with her shoulder. This time it closed. Both torches remained lit on the shelf for Shen Tong to collect on his return.

**Conditions and results:** limited light changes how she sees the third tray. The hose affects access and closure, so moving it enables the door to close. Shen Tong’s help is established at the start. Permission to use the room does not prove long-term accommodation for the seedlings. Research safety or horticultural details separately if the manuscript needs them.

Smell, temperature and still description can also build atmosphere and experience without triggering new events. Choose details for the reading goal rather than filling a sensory quota.

heading.zh: 环境描写显得水，怎样删改
heading.en: How to Cut or Revise Setting Description That Feels Like Padding

body.zh:
| 症状 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 天气开场与人物、气氛和本场重心都无关 | 可从受天气影响的动作进入；若静景有明确作用，也可保留 |
| 罗列颜色、声音、气味，彼此无关 | 留下会影响判断或节奏的一两项 |
| 所有人都注意同样的景色 | 按人物目标与经验筛选细节 |
| 环境只负责象征人物心情 | 先判断象征是否有效；缺现场依据再补已有细节 |
| 场景条件写过后不再生效 | 检查是否影响体验或后续；无功能才删 |
| 为了“不水”把地点删成空白 | 保留行动所需的距离、出口、障碍与可操作物 |

环境少写不等于不写。读者需要知道动作能否发生、危险从哪里来、人物能碰到什么。删的是不参与体验的清单，不是空间因果。
body.en:
| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| A weather opening has no connection to the characters, atmosphere, or scene focus | Consider entering through weather affecting action; keep a still opening when it serves a clear purpose |
| Colors, sounds, and smells are listed without connection | Keep the one or two details that alter judgment or rhythm |
| Everyone notices the same view | Filter details through each character’s goal and experience |
| The setting only symbolizes a character’s mood | Assess the symbolism; restore existing detail if it lacks support in the scene |
| A condition never matters after it is described | Check its effect on experience and later events; cut only if it has no function |
| In avoiding padding, the writer strips the location into a blank | Preserve distances, exits, obstacles, and usable objects required for action |

Writing less setting does not mean writing none. Readers need to know whether an action is possible, where danger comes from, and what the character can reach. Remove the list that does not participate in experience, not the spatial cause and effect.

q.zh: 环境描写一定要推动剧情吗？
q.en: Must every setting description advance the plot?

a.zh: 不必每句都制造事件。它也可以建立气氛、节奏和人物体验；但应改变读者对现场的感受或理解。纯重复已知气氛、删掉无损的装饰可以压缩。
a.en: No. Description can also establish atmosphere, rhythm, and character experience, but it should change how readers feel or understand the scene. Decoration that merely repeats a known mood and can be removed without loss may be compressed.

q.zh: 五感是不是写得越多越有画面？
q.en: Does using more senses always make a scene more vivid?

a.zh: 不是。选择人物此刻最敏感、最能影响动作的感受即可。感官齐全却没有注意重点，反而会冲淡画面。
a.en: No. Choose the sensation the character is most sensitive to now and that most affects the action. Covering every sense without a focus can dilute the image instead.

text.zh: 用 /story-long-write（Codex 用 $story-long-write）局部修订环境描写，附人物目标、既定场景条件与本书文风。保留影响行动或体验的细节，不新增权限、协助者、工具或物理结果；不凑五感，也不要求每句景物制造事件。
text.en: Use /story-long-write, or $story-long-write in Codex, for a local setting revision with goals, established conditions and book style. Preserve details affecting action or experience. Add no permission, helpers, tools or physical results; require neither sensory quotas nor an event from every detail.

title.zh: 小说改短剧怎么删角色、合并角色：先保住人物功能
title.en: Short Drama: Preserve Character Function Before Cutting or Merging

seo_title.zh: 小说改短剧怎么删角色与合并角色｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Merge Characters for Short Drama | ZenStory

description.zh: 短剧改编压缩人物，先删不保留的支线，再按行动、信息、关系与因果功能判断是否合并，并修复知情范围和铺垫。附原创展馆案例。
description.en: Cut subplots first, then merge characters by action, information, relationships, and causality. Includes a function ledger and an original gallery example.

answer.zh: 删角色前先列出他迫使谁选择、掌握什么信息、处在什么关系位置，以及为后文建立了哪条因果。先决定整条支线是否保留，再处理人物合并。只有两个角色的功能能由同一个目标、知情范围和关系位置自洽承担时才合并；转移出去的证据、许可、反对或牺牲要写明由谁接住。人物变少不是成功标准，因果不断、冲突不塌、观众不会提前知道答案才是。
answer.en: Before cutting a character, list whom they force to choose, what information they hold, where they stand in the relationship map, and which later cause and effect depends on them. Decide whether an entire subplot remains before merging characters. Merge only when one coherent goal, knowledge boundary, and relationship position can carry both characters’ functions. State who inherits any transferred evidence, permission, opposition, or sacrifice. Fewer characters is not the measure of success; causality must remain intact, conflict must survive, and the audience must not learn answers too early.

heading.zh: 先为候选角色做一张人物作用表
heading.en: Start with a Function Ledger for Every Candidate Character

body.zh:
| 角色 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| 姓名或称呼 | 迫使谁作选择: 造成哪次决定; 独有信息或资源: 证据、权限、技能、误信; 关系位置: 亲属、债主、同事、对手等; 后续依赖: 哪个揭示或结果需要他 |

“负责搞笑”“戏份不多”不足以决定去留。一个只出现两场的人，可能是主角取得许可证的唯一来源；一个出现很多次的人，也可能只重复别人已经完成的说明。先写功能，再讨论删、并或换载体。

这是本文的编辑检查表，不是原生改编映射的完整格式。情绪、声线、陪伴和节奏也是功能；人物没有提供新线索，不等于可以删。
body.en:
| Role | Function |
|---|---|
| Name or role | Choice: Which decision do they cause?; Information: Evidence, access, skill, or false belief; Relationship: Relative, creditor, colleague, opponent, and so on; Later need: Which revelation or result requires them? |

“Provides comic relief” and “has few scenes” are not enough to decide whether someone stays. A person appearing in only two scenes may be the protagonist’s sole route to a permit. Someone with many appearances may merely repeat an explanation already delivered by others. Write the functions before discussing deletion, combination, or a different carrier.

This is an editorial worksheet, not the complete native adaptation-map format. Emotion, voice, companionship, and rhythm are functions too. A character need not supply a new clue to be worth keeping.

heading.zh: 压缩顺序：先删线，再合并人物
heading.en: Compression Order: Cut Plotlines Before Merging Characters

body.zh:
先问某条支线是否仍属于这版短剧的核心承诺。若整条线删除，就把它的铺垫、兑现和孤儿线索一起处理，并逐项决定其中功能是随线删除，还是转移给保留线。

之后才合并人物。否则刚把证据和关系搬到某人身上，又发现他的整条线不保留，会造成重复返工。删线也不能只看节奏快慢：有些慢场建立信任、取得手段或制造信息差，删掉后，后面的快场虽然还在，却失去成立条件。
body.en:
First ask whether a subplot still belongs to the core promise of this short-drama version. If you remove the entire line, handle its setup, payoff, and orphaned clues together. For each function within it, decide whether it disappears with the line or transfers to a retained one.

Only then merge characters. Otherwise, you may move evidence and relationships onto someone whose entire line is later removed, creating duplicate work. Do not cut a subplot merely because it is slower. Some slow scenes establish trust, secure a means, or create an information gap; remove them and the later fast scenes may remain while losing the conditions that make them work.

heading.zh: 合并前过五道检查
heading.en: Pass Five Checks Before a Merge

body.zh:
1. **目标**：同一个人能否同时想要这两件事，还是会自相矛盾？
2. **知情范围**：合并后是否会让秘密提前泄露，或让人物知道来源不明的事实？
3. **关系位置**：支持者与施压者若合成一人，原有对抗是否消失？
4. **行动条件**：同一人在时间和空间上能否完成两项关键行动？
5. **代价**：原本的背叛、证言、拒绝或牺牲，会不会因为合并而失去重量？

若只有部分功能能合并，不必强求“二合一”。可以合并日常事务，却把独有证据转给另一个已经保留、且有合理取得路径的角色。
body.en:
1. **Goal:** Can one person coherently want both things, or do the desires contradict each other?
2. **Knowledge boundary:** Does the merge reveal a secret early or give the character a fact with no source?
3. **Relationship position:** If supporter and pressure source become one person, does the original opposition disappear?
4. **Conditions for action:** Can one person perform both crucial actions within the story’s time and space?
5. **Cost:** Does the original betrayal, testimony, refusal, or sacrifice lose weight after the merge?

If only some functions combine, do not force a complete two-into-one merge. Routine tasks can be merged while exclusive evidence moves to another retained character who has a plausible way to obtain it.

heading.zh: 原创范例：闭馆前的社区展厅
heading.en: Original Example: A Community Gallery Before Closing

body.zh:
以下是完整虚构输入与候选方案。青年策展人顾葵要在展厅次晨交回前保存社区口述资料。原作四名配角各有作用：老任负责夜间接待，可以按馆内已定规则登记进入申请；物业主管只在白天接待；小禾帮助整理目录，发现编号页缺失，但没有进入许可权；周总听过公开展出的工伤证言，以续租为条件要求撤下它。老任另有寻找失散战友录音的支线。

这版已选择以资料保存和证言去留为主线，因此提议删去寻战友的照片、查询与团聚。若作品的核心承诺本来就是老任与战友重逢，就不能仅为少一个人删掉；删线仍须保住主线依赖的夜间许可。

一种失败合并是：把老任并入小禾，并直接写“已经答应整理的小禾也已批准顾葵入馆”。这跳过了原来需要争取许可的选择，且把目录知识与批准集中在开场。问题在这份具体方案，不是保安与整理员永远不能由同一人承担；若保留各项行动的时点、目标和拒绝理由，也可以另作可行版本。

本文候选保留小禾与周总，把老任的夜间接待功能转给物业主管。不是因为“物业主管”称呼便能开夜门：映射写明他接住夜间值班职责及相应许可范围；原来白天接待的功能保留，他仍没听过未公开录音。新增夜班安排是改编选择，需要作者接受，不能冒称原著已有此人夜间值班。

在已接受这个候选的示范中，顾葵向主管申请本夜核对资料，主管询问要查看的盒号；小禾从目录报出编号，没有替顾葵批准。主管实际登记，并同意两人入内核对；资料的带走仍须另作清单，登记进入不等于已获全部转移许可。顾葵因此先核对，下一步再争取保存与展出安排。次晨交回展厅的期限和周总的撤展要求继续存在，没有凭空追加“违反消防规定就封存全部展品”。

人数从四个配角变三个，权限、目录信息和撤展压力仍分开；顾葵仍要提出请求、接收条件和处理不同立场。夜班安排改变了什么、原支线损失了什么，也都交作者判断，而不是用“压缩成功”遮住。
body.en:
The input and candidate here are entirely fictional. Curator Gu Kui wants to preserve community oral-history material before the gallery is handed back the next morning. Four supporting characters perform different functions. Old Ren handles night access and can register entry requests under the gallery's established rule. A property manager handles daytime entry only. Xiao He helps catalog the material and discovers a missing numbered page, but cannot grant access. Sponsor Mr. Zhou has heard the publicly exhibited workplace-injury testimony and demands its removal as a condition of renewal. Old Ren also searches the recordings for a lost comrade.

This adaptation has chosen preservation and the fate of the testimony as its main line, so it proposes dropping the search photographs, inquiries, and reunion. If Old Ren's reunion were the work's core promise, cutting it merely to reduce cast would fail. Removing that line must still preserve the nighttime permission needed by the main plot.

One failed merger puts Old Ren's function into Xiao He and simply declares that “Xiao He, who agreed to catalog, has also approved Gu's entry.” That skips the original choice of seeking permission and concentrates knowledge and approval at the opening. The defect belongs to that proposal, not to an absolute ban on merging a guard and cataloger. A different version can work if it preserves the timing, goals, and reasons for refusing each action.

This candidate retains Xiao He and Zhou, transferring Old Ren's night-entry function to the property manager. The job title alone does not grant night access. The mapping explicitly transfers the night duty and its permission scope while retaining daytime reception; the manager still has not heard the unpublished recordings. Assigning him a night shift is an adaptation choice for the author to accept, not an existing source fact about his schedule.

In the demonstration after that choice is accepted, Gu asks to examine material that night. The manager asks which box; Xiao He supplies its catalog number without approving entry for Gu. The manager actually registers the request and agrees to let both in to check. Taking material away still requires a separate list; entry does not grant unrestricted transfer permission. Gu checks first and must next seek preservation and display arrangements. The morning handover and Zhou's demand remain, without inventing a threat to seal every exhibit for a fire-rule breach.

Four supporting roles become three, but permission, catalog knowledge, and pressure to remove testimony remain distinct. Gu still makes requests, receives conditions, and faces different positions. Changes to the night shift and losses from the removed subplot remain author decisions rather than disappearing behind a claim that compression succeeded.

heading.zh: 删并之后，逐项修复因果桥
heading.en: Repair Every Causal Bridge After Cuts and Merges

body.zh:
用一条链回读每项重要结果：原因事实 → 人物怎样知道 → 作出什么选择 → 对方怎样反制 → 产生什么可见后果。角色删除后，最容易断在“怎样知道”和“怎样获得”。不能用一句“她早有准备”跨过去。

| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 因为名字多就合并 | 先比较功能、目标和关系位置 |
| 证人并入反派后仍保留秘密 | 重分信息来源，避免人物自我隐瞒 |
| 删除慢支线，主角突然拿到证据 | 为证据建立新的取得行动与代价 |
| 合并支持者和反对者，冲突消失 | 保留不同立场，或让其他关系承担压力 |
| 所有功能都塞给主角 | 保留需要他人许可、反制或独立选择的部分 |
| 删掉人物却留下无人兑现的伏笔 | 同步删除或明确转移每条铺垫 |

最后把每项改动写成“原功能 → 新承载者或删除 → 保住什么 → 损失什么”。若损失触及核心关系、关键选择或结局含义，应回退合并，不要靠对白解释。
body.en:
Read each important result back through one chain: causal fact → how a character learns it → what choice they make → how the other side counters → what visible consequence follows. After a character is removed, the chain most often breaks at “how they learn it” or “how they obtain it.” “She was prepared all along” cannot bridge the gap.

| Failure | Fix |
|---|---|
| Merging characters because there are too many names | Compare functions, goals, and relationship positions first |
| A witness is merged into the antagonist, yet the secret remains | Reassign the information source so the character is not hiding a fact from themself |
| A slow subplot is removed and the protagonist suddenly has the evidence | Establish a new action and cost through which the evidence is obtained |
| A supporter and opponent merge, erasing conflict | Keep the positions separate or let another relationship carry the pressure |
| Every function is assigned to the protagonist | Retain functions requiring another person’s permission, countermove, or independent choice |
| A character is removed but their setup remains with no payoff | Delete or explicitly transfer every setup at the same time |

Finally, write every change as: “original function → new carrier or deletion → what is preserved → what is lost.” If the loss affects a core relationship, crucial choice, or the ending’s meaning, reverse the merge rather than explaining it through dialogue.

q.zh: 短剧角色是不是越少越好？
q.en: Should a short drama always have as few characters as possible?

a.zh: 不是。角色数量服从故事功能和制作条件。删到同一人既提供证据、又制造阻力、又承担所有反应，容易让关系扁平或信息穿帮。
a.en: No. Cast size serves story function and production conditions. If one person supplies the evidence, creates the obstacle, and carries every reaction, relationships may flatten and knowledge boundaries may break.

q.zh: 两个作用相似的配角一定能合并吗？
q.en: Can two supporting characters with similar functions always be merged?

a.zh: 还要检查目标、知情范围、关系历史、时空条件和代价。都负责提供线索，但一人是亲属、一人是竞争者，合并可能改变主角为何相信这条线索。
a.en: You must also check goals, knowledge boundaries, relationship history, time and place, and cost. Two characters may both provide clues, but if one is family and the other a rival, merging them can change why the protagonist believes the clue.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中用 /short-drama-develop（Codex 中用 `$short-drama-develop`）只做人物压缩方案：按实际原著列角色的行动、信息、关系与因果功能，先标出可删支线，再检查合并后的知情范围和代价，并输出原功能到新承载者的对应；暂不写剧本。
text.en: In Claude Code, use `/short-drama-develop` only to create a character-compression plan. From the actual source novel, list each character’s action, information, relationship, and causal functions. Mark removable subplots first, then check knowledge boundaries and costs after each merge, and map every original function to its new carrier. Do not write the script yet. In Codex, use `$short-drama-develop`.

label.zh: 改编功能、合并与新增登记

title.zh: 短剧证据镜头怎么拍：让观众看清，也看见后果
title.en: How to Shoot Evidence Reveals: Make the Proof and Consequences Clear

seo_title.zh: 短剧证据镜头怎么拍｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Shoot Evidence Reveals in Short Drama | ZenStory

description.zh: 文件、手机、伤痕或物件成为证据时，先确定观众必须读到哪项特征，再安排控制权、揭示、接收反应和行动后果。附原创药房案例。
description.en: Define the feature viewers must read, then stage control, reveal, reaction, and consequence. Includes a pharmacy example with two temperature logs.

answer.zh: 证据镜头先回答五件事：证据在哪里、谁控制它、观众在揭示前知道什么、真正证明结论的是文字、形状、状态还是人物与物件的关系，以及谁看见后会改变行动。镜头无需按固定数量排列，但要给关键特征足够的尺度和时间，并让取得证据、读懂证据与证据造成的后果各有承载。
answer.en: An evidence shot must answer five questions: Where is the evidence? Who controls it? What does the audience know before the reveal? Is the conclusion proved by text, shape, condition, or the relationship between a person and an object? Who changes course after seeing it? The shots need no fixed count, but the decisive feature needs enough scale and screen time, while obtaining the evidence, understanding it, and acting on it each need a clear carrier.

heading.zh: 先确定证据究竟证明什么
heading.en: First Define Exactly What the Evidence Proves

body.zh:
“拍一张文件特写”仍不够具体。先写出观众必须得到的最小事实：是日期早于事故、签名与本人笔迹不符、包装封口已断，还是手机在某时仍连接现场网络。

| 证据类型 | 必须看清的东西 |
|---|---|
| 精确文字 | 具体词句、日期、号码或名字 |
| 形状与状态 | 断角、划痕、封口、缺页、开合 |
| 对照差异 | 两个版本之间唯一关键变化 |
| 关系证据 | 谁持有、谁能接触、物件出现在何处 |

一项证据通常只能支持有限判断。看见断封只能证明封口被动过，无法单独确定操作者或动机。
body.en:
“Shoot a close-up of the document” is still too vague. State the minimum fact the audience must learn: Is the date earlier than the accident? Does the signature differ from the person’s handwriting? Is the package seal broken? Was the phone still connected to the network at the location at a certain time?

| Evidence type | What must be legible |
|---|---|
| Exact text | A specific phrase, date, number, or name |
| Shape and condition | A broken corner, scratch, seal, missing page, or open/closed state |
| Comparative difference | The single decisive change between two versions |
| Relational evidence | Who holds it, who had access, or where the object appears |

One piece of evidence usually supports only a limited inference. A broken seal proves that the seal was disturbed; it cannot identify the person responsible or their motive by itself.

heading.zh: 把揭示拆成信息变化，而非镜头配额
heading.en: Break the Reveal into Changes in Information, Not a Shot Quota

body.zh:
证据场面可能包含方位、取得、展示、理解、反应和后果，但不要求六个镜头。先按信息变化组织：

- 建立证据与人物的空间关系；
- 某人取得、打开或让它进入可见状态；
- 观众读到关键特征；
- 接收者的判断发生变化；
- 新判断改变持物、站位、对白或下一动作。

两项变化能在同一双人镜里读清，就不必硬切。只有注意、解释、控制权或关系真的变化时再切镜。
body.en:
An evidence scene may involve position, acquisition, display, understanding, reaction, and consequence, but it does not require six shots. Organize it by changes in information:

- Establish the spatial relationship between the evidence and the characters.
- Let someone obtain it, open it, or make it visible.
- Let the audience read the decisive feature.
- Change the recipient’s judgment.
- Let the new judgment alter possession, position, dialogue, or the next action.

If two changes read clearly in one two-shot, do not cut merely to fill a pattern. Cut when attention, interpretation, control, or a relationship actually changes.

heading.zh: 文字证据与物件证据的可读方式不同
heading.en: Textual Evidence and Physical Evidence Need Different Readability

body.zh:
精确文字是证据时，先确认文字有准确版本，再选择直接呈现或后期排字；镜头要让承载面正对、无遮挡，并给观众读完的时间。一闪而过的手机屏不能只靠台词宣称“大家都看清了”。

若证据是纹样、裂口或物件位置，画面应强调这一特征，不要临时生成无关文字。证据被拿起、翻面或递交时，还要保持上一镜的持有人、方向和状态，避免关键特征在切镜后换边或消失。
body.en:
When exact wording is evidence, first establish an accurate text version, then choose whether to show it directly or typeset it in post. The surface should face the camera without obstruction, and viewers need enough time to read it. A phone screen that flashes past cannot become legible merely because a line of dialogue says that everyone saw it.

When the evidence is a pattern, crack, or object position, emphasize that feature instead of generating unrelated text. If someone picks up, turns over, or hands off the evidence, preserve the holder, orientation, and condition from the previous shot so the decisive feature does not switch sides or disappear after the cut.

heading.zh: 范例：排练室的两份停电记录
heading.en: Example: Two Outage Records in a Rehearsal Room

body.zh:
**原创设定**：社区排练室一次预订在停电中被打断。管理员周齐拿手写签，说只有最后十分钟停电，应只按十分钟核算补时；预约者陈澜不接受这个解释。工作人员于芮已有查看本室供电日志的职责，日志面板在桌后，记录装置在本例中专门记录这间房的供电区间；补时需值班负责人核对后确认。镜头不把这份日志当成所有设备或整栋楼情况的证明。

**镜头一，三人中景**：周齐在桌前举手写签，于芮能到日志面板，陈澜站桌旁等待核对。建立证据位置、持有与合法的取得途径，不安排她绕过锁去取资料。

**镜头二，跟随于芮的近景**：她调出这次预订日期的日志，将已有打印功能输出的记录拿到桌上。负责取得，日期先核准；尚未要求观众读完全部数字。

**镜头三，两份记录同框**：已定文字版本是日志“16:20–17:20”、手写签“17:10–17:20”。两者在同一日期并排可读，显示日志覆盖一小时、手写签只记最后十分钟。若采用后期排字，先完成这两块承载面的字形、透视和停留，不在空白画面上说已经完成对照。

**镜头四，三人中景**：陈澜指向缺失的前段，拒绝按十分钟结束核算；周齐把手写签放到桌上，没有销毁或换版。于芮按既有流程联系值班负责人，展示两份记录；对方回复先撤下十分钟的暂算，核对此次预订再确认补时。于芮在登记中实际标明待核算。

观众看见依据如何取得、范围怎样不同，以及一次决定真正被改变。日志区间不一致还不能单独证明周齐故意造假；补时待核算也不等于陈澜已经得到补用的一小时。需要把这项回报结清时，后场再写确认、预约和实际使用。
body.en:
**Original setup:** A community rehearsal-room booking is interrupted by an outage. Administrator Zhou Qi holds a handwritten slip, claiming only the last ten minutes were affected and should count toward replacement time. Booker Chen Lan disputes it. Staff member Yu Rui already has responsibility for reading this room’s power log at a panel behind the desk. In this fictional setup the device records this room’s supply intervals. A duty lead must check and approve replacement time. The log does not establish conditions in every device or the entire building.

**Shot one, three-person medium:** Zhou holds the slip at the desk; Yu has a route to the log panel; Chen waits beside the desk. Establish location, possession, and an authorized acquisition route rather than breaking into locked records.

**Shot two, closer with Yu:** She selects the booking date and brings the existing panel’s printed record to the desk. This acquires the second source and checks its date without asking viewers to read every number yet.

**Shot three, both records together:** Approved wording is “16:20–17:20” on the log and “17:10–17:20” on the slip, side by side for the same date. One covers an hour, the other its last ten minutes. If text is composited, complete wording, perspective, and reading time on both surfaces rather than announce a comparison over blank papers.

**Shot four, three-person medium:** Chen points to the missing earlier interval and refuses to end the calculation at ten minutes. Zhou sets the slip on the desk without destroying or replacing it. Yu contacts the duty lead under the established procedure and presents both records. The lead replies that the provisional ten-minute figure should be withdrawn while this booking is checked. Yu actually marks recalculation pending in the register.

Viewers see acquisition, differing scope, and an enacted decision change. The mismatch alone does not prove deliberate falsification. Pending calculation is not an hour of replacement rehearsal already received. A later scene can deliver approval, booking, and actual use if the story needs that payoff settled.

heading.zh: 证据镜头常见失效
heading.en: Common Ways Evidence Shots Fail

body.zh:
| 失效 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 只有文件特写，不知道它证明什么 | 写出最小事实与结论边界 |
| 观众还没读完就切走 | 调整尺度、遮挡和停留，或拆出可读镜头 |
| 人物念完全文代替画面 | 只说争议点，让画面承担可见依据 |
| 揭示后所有人轮流震惊 | 选会改变风险的代表反应或群体状态 |
| 证据切镜后换手、翻面或变版本 | 对齐上一镜终点与下一镜起点 |
| 证据出现后行动没有变化 | 让判断落到拒绝、追问、封存、交出或离场 |
body.en:
| Failure | Fix |
|---|---|
| A document gets a close-up, but no one knows what it proves | State the minimum fact and the boundary of the inference |
| The shot cuts before viewers finish reading | Adjust scale, obstruction, and duration, or separate a readable shot |
| A character reads the entire document aloud instead of letting the image work | Speak only the disputed point and let the visible evidence support it |
| Everyone takes turns looking shocked after the reveal | Choose the representative reaction or group-state change that alters risk |
| After a cut, the evidence changes hands, flips, or becomes another version | Match the ending state of one shot to the starting state of the next |
| Nothing changes after the evidence appears | Turn the judgment into a refusal, question, hold, surrender, or departure |

q.zh: 证据一定要给特写吗？
q.en: Does evidence always need a close-up?

a.zh: 不需要。若证据在谁手里、谁拒绝接触更重要，中景或双人镜更清楚；只有关键特征太小、必须单独读取时才收近。
a.en: No. If who holds the evidence or who refuses to touch it matters more, a medium shot or two-shot may be clearer. Move closer only when the decisive feature is too small and must be read on its own.

q.zh: 手机聊天记录应该全部拍出来吗？
q.en: Should a phone chat be shown in full?

a.zh: 只呈现当前结论必需的消息、时间或发送者，并保证文字版本准确。无关长对话会延长阅读并增加制作负担。
a.en: Show only the message, time, or sender required for the present conclusion, and make sure the text version is accurate. Irrelevant long exchanges increase reading time and production work.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中用 /short-drama-storyboard（Codex 中用 `$short-drama-storyboard`）只设计这个证据揭示：写清证据控制者、观众必须读到的最小事实、呈现尺度、谁先看见、接收反应和后续行动；不改证据内容，不扩到全片分镜。
text.en: In Claude Code, use `/short-drama-storyboard` only to design this evidence reveal. Specify who controls the evidence, the minimum fact viewers must read, presentation scale, who sees it first, the recipient’s reaction, and the resulting action. Do not change the evidence or expand into a full-film storyboard. In Codex, use `$short-drama-storyboard`.

label.zh: 可见性、景别与动作连续

title.zh: AI 视频道具不一致怎么办：参考图模板与示例
title.en: How to Create Prop References for AI Video

seo_title.zh: AI 视频道具不一致怎么办：参考图模板与示例
seo_title.en: How to Create Prop References for AI Video

description.zh: 可复用道具参考图先固定尺度、轮廓、材质和功能件，再单列当前开合、损伤、内容物与文字方式。附原创录音机参考板。
description.en: Fix a prop’s scale, form, materials, and working parts; list current open/closed state, damage, contents, and text separately. Includes a recorder board.

answer.zh: AI短剧道具参考图要先固定不会随一场动作轻易改变的身份：尺度、主要比例、轮廓、材料、接缝、开口与功能件；再单列当前状态，例如开合、损伤、污渍、内容物和文字版本。选择足以识别结构的正侧视或局部视图，并为可读文字、图形符号、空白承载面或后期排字选一种处理。参考图只展示已确定状态，不提前演完剧情动作。
answer.en: For an AI short-drama prop reference, first fix the identity that should not change casually with one scene’s action: scale, major proportions, silhouette, materials, seams, openings, and functional parts. Then specify the current state, such as open or closed, damage, stains, contents, and text version. Choose front, side, or detail views that make the structure recognizable. For text, choose one treatment: accurately readable wording, graphic marks, a blank surface, or later typesetting. A reference image shows an established state; it should not perform the entire story action in advance.

heading.zh: 先分清道具身份与当前状态
heading.en: Separate the Prop’s Lasting Identity from Its Current State

body.zh:
| 层次 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 持久身份 | 固定: 尺度、轮廓、比例、材料、功能结构、永久磨损; 示例: 铰链方向、把手形状、固定缺口 |
| 当前状态 | 固定: 开合、损伤、污渍、内容物、持有关系、文字版本; 示例: 盖子打开、磁带在内、标签已撕半 |

换手、打开或沾水通常只是人物处境变化，不应重新设计成另一件道具。真正改变形制和功能的不可逆改造，才需要另行决定是否建立新版身份。
body.en:
| Layer | Contents |
|---|---|
| Lasting identity | Keep: Scale, silhouette, proportions, materials, functional structure, and permanent wear; Example: Hinge direction, handle shape, fixed notch |
| Current state | Keep: Open or closed, damage, stains, contents, who holds it, and text version; Example: Lid open, cassette inside, label half torn away |

Changing hands, opening, or getting wet is usually a state change and should not redesign the item into a different prop. Only an irreversible modification that truly changes its form and function calls for deciding whether to establish a new identity version.

heading.zh: 一张可复用道具板写哪些信息
heading.en: What to Include on a Reusable Prop Board

body.zh:
按使用目的选择必要项：

1. 道具类型与剧情用途；
2. 真实尺度或中性参照，以及长宽厚比例；
3. 主材、次材、反光、透明或粗糙关系；
4. 接缝、扣件、开口、握持面和活动方向；
5. 当前损伤、内容物与表面状态；
6. 正面、侧面、背面或关键局部中真正有用的视图；
7. 文字承载面怎样处理；
8. 需要保持与排除的变形、错材、错状态和多余复制品。

尺度参照优先使用无身份的常见物或明确尺寸关系，避免让某个剧情人物的手成为默认参考，从而把人物也粘进道具资产。
body.en:
Choose only what the intended use requires:

1. Prop type and story function.
2. Real scale or a neutral reference, plus length-width-thickness proportions.
3. Primary and secondary materials, including reflective, transparent, and rough relationships.
4. Seams, fasteners, openings, grip surfaces, and directions of movement.
5. Current damage, contents, and surface state.
6. Only the useful front, side, back, or key detail views.
7. The treatment for any text-bearing surface.
8. Deformations, wrong materials, wrong states, and extra duplicate props that must be excluded.

Prefer an identity-neutral common object or an explicit size relationship as the scale reference. Avoid using a story character’s hand by default, which can bind that character into the prop asset as well.

heading.zh: 道具上的字先选处理方式
heading.en: Choose How to Handle Text on the Prop First

body.zh:
- **准确可读**：剧情要求观众逐字读懂，保存确定文本及承载位置。
- **图形存在**：只需看到标签或刻痕的布局，不产生可辨的新名字和号码。
- **保持空白**：本轮画面不应出现字，同时保留承载面的材质与透视。
- **后期添加**：先留无遮挡、可跟踪透视的干净区域，准确文字在后期完成。

这些方式不能同时套在同一承载面。选择后期排字，不等于最终镜头可以忘记补字；选择准确可读，也不能再全局要求“不要任何文字”。

先保留视觉设定中“最终需准确可读、只作图形、不应可读、文字待定”的决定，再选择这张板如何呈现。资产要求与本轮参考板的排字方式不是同一层：后期添加可以服务最终准确文字；未定文本仍须保留待确认，提示词作者不补编。
body.en:
- **Accurately readable:** The plot requires viewers to read the wording exactly, so preserve the approved text and its location.
- **Graphic presence:** The label or engraving layout must be visible, without generating a legible new name or number.
- **Keep blank:** No text should appear in this image, while the material and perspective of the text-bearing surface remain.
- **Add in post:** Leave a clean, unobstructed area with trackable perspective, then add exact text during post-production.

These treatments cannot all apply to the same surface. Choosing later typesetting does not mean the final shot may forget to add the text. Choosing accurately readable wording cannot coexist with a global instruction to remove all text.

Preserve the visual setting's decision about final exact text, graphic presence, no readable text, or text still undecided, then choose how this plate presents it. The asset requirement and this reference image's lettering method are different layers. Later lettering may serve final exact text; undecided content must remain pending rather than being invented by the prompt writer.

heading.zh: 原创范例：档案采访用的便携录音机
heading.en: Original Example: A Portable Recorder for Archive Interviews

body.zh:
虚构故事用旧录音机播放一盒采访磁带。录音机的可复用身份为：巴掌宽的扁长机身，深绿色磨砂塑料；左侧银色滑杆，正面双圆轴窗，底部电池盖有斜向裂缝，右上角网罩凹陷。比例、裂缝与滑杆位置保持，采访内容属于磁带，不凭空存进空仓机身。

状态A是“合盖、空仓、滑杆在停止位”；状态B是“仓盖打开，透明磁带在内，左卷带量较少”。默认分开成明确状态图，若作者需要对照板，须分区标清，不能在同一物体同一时点混用开与关、空与满。磁带另外追踪，装入录音机只改变它的位置和录音机的内容状态。

剧情要求后续读到采访编号，但本例没有提供逐字文本，编号仍待作者确定。B图给磁带标签留清楚、无遮挡的区域，当前采用后期排字的准备方式；A图没有磁带，不能凭空画出同一标签。确认准确编号后再将文字与来源写入视觉设定并完成后期，最终镜头核对可读结果。预留空白不是编号已定或成片已经可读；机身原有模糊品牌位仅保留几何凹槽，不编新名字。

视图按需要选择：正面固定轮廓与轴窗；侧面固定滑杆和厚度；开仓局部显示铰链与磁带方向；底部裂缝若是后续识别点，另给可看清底部的局部，不把顶面开仓视图说成能同时看见底面。参考板展示结构和已定状态，具体拨动滑杆及转带过程留给镜头。
body.en:
A fictional story uses an old recorder to play an interview cassette. Its reusable identity is a palm-width, flattened rectangular body in dark-green matte plastic; a silver slider on the left, two round front reel windows, a diagonal crack in the bottom battery cover, and a dented grille at the top right. Keep the proportions, crack, and slider position. The interview belongs to the cassette rather than being stored in an empty recorder body.

State A is “lid closed, compartment empty, slider at stop.” State B is “lid open, transparent cassette inside, less tape on the left reel.” Separate state images are the default. An author may request a comparison board with clearly labeled areas, but one object at one moment cannot be both open and closed or empty and full. Track the cassette separately; insertion changes its location and the recorder's contents.

The plot needs a readable interview number later, but this example supplies no exact text, so the number remains for the author to decide. Image B reserves a clear, unobstructed cassette-label area for later lettering; image A has no cassette and must not invent that label. Once the exact number is confirmed, record the text and source in the visual setting, complete post-production, and check readability in the final shot. An empty area establishes neither a decided number nor readable final footage. The recorder's indistinct brand area retains only a geometric recess, without inventing a name.

Choose views for use: front for silhouette and reel windows, side for slider and thickness, open-compartment detail for hinge and tape direction. If the bottom crack is a later recognition point, add a detail that can actually see the underside rather than claiming a top opening view shows it too. The plate shows structure and an established state; moving the slider and turning the reels belong to the shot.

heading.zh: 道具参考图常见失败
heading.en: Common Prop Reference Failures

body.zh:
| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 只写“古老、精致、神秘” | 补尺度、轮廓、材料和功能结构 |
| 开、关、完好、破损同时出现 | 每张状态图只选一个明确时点 |
| 不同视图里缺口和活动件换位 | 先固定身份锚点与视图方向 |
| 用角色手作比例，人物也被复制 | 改用中性参照或明确尺寸关系 |
| 临时编造标签文字 | 选择准确文本、图形、空白或后期方式 |
| 为展示功能直接演完剧情动作 | 参考板展示结构和起始状态，动作留给镜头 |
body.en:
| Failure | Fix |
|---|---|
| The prompt says only “old, exquisite, mysterious” | Add scale, silhouette, materials, and functional structure |
| Open, closed, intact, and damaged states appear together | Choose one clear moment for each state image |
| Notches and moving parts shift between views | Fix identity anchors and viewing directions first |
| A character’s hand sets scale, so the person is duplicated too | Use a neutral reference or explicit size relationship |
| The system invents temporary label text | Choose exact text, graphics, blank space, or post-production |
| The board performs the plot action to demonstrate function | Show structure and starting state; leave action to the shot |

q.zh: 一个道具需要画几个视图？
q.en: How many views does one prop need?

a.zh: 看识别与使用需要。正面足以固定轮廓时无需凑视图；背部机关、开启方向或关键损伤不可见时，再加侧面、背面或局部。
a.en: Use only the views required for recognition and use. If the front fixes the silhouette, do not add views to meet a quota. Add a side, back, or detail only when a rear mechanism, opening direction, or crucial damage is otherwise invisible.

q.zh: 道具坏了以后要重新做参考图吗？
q.en: Do I need a new reference image after the prop is damaged?

a.zh: 身份不变、损伤需要跨镜保持时，新增损坏状态参考即可。若损伤彻底改变形制或功能，再决定是否建立新版身份。
a.en: If its identity remains the same and the damage must persist across shots, add a damaged-state reference. If the damage fundamentally changes form or function, then decide whether to create a new identity version.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中用 /short-drama-image-prompts（Codex 中用 `$short-drama-image-prompts`）为这个已确定道具整理参考图提示词：分开持久身份与当前状态，写尺度、轮廓、材料、功能件、必要视图和文字处理；只做参考板，不生成剧情动作。
text.en: In Claude Code, use `/short-drama-image-prompts` to prepare reference-image prompts for this established prop. Separate lasting identity from current state, and specify scale, silhouette, materials, functional parts, necessary views, and text treatment. Create only the reference-board prompt, not a story action. In Codex, use `$short-drama-image-prompts`.

title.zh: 短剧内心戏怎么写：把心理活动变成可表演信息
title.en: How to Write Inner Monologue for Short Drama: Make It Performable

seo_title.zh: 短剧内心戏怎么写｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Write Inner Monologue for Short Drama | ZenStory

description.zh: 小说心理描写改成短剧时，先保留它改变选择的作用，再在行动、证据、空间、对白与有意旁白中选载体。附原创冷库案例。
description.en: Preserve how a thought changes a choice, then carry it through action, evidence, space, dialogue, or deliberate voice-over. Includes a cold-room example.

answer.zh: 把小说心理活动改成短剧，先写清这层内心使人物怎样判断、选择或隐瞒，再选择观众能接收的载体。优先让行动后果、证据反应、空间位置或关系动作承担意义；确实需要把私人想法直接交给观众时，再有意使用内心声音。无论选择哪种方式，都要分清观众听见了什么、现场其他人物是否听见，以及这条信息怎样改变下一步。
answer.en: When adapting internal narration from a novel into short drama, first state how the thought changes what the character judges, chooses, or conceals. Then choose a carrier the audience can receive. Prefer consequences of action, responses to evidence, spatial position, or relational action. Use an inner voice deliberately when a private thought must reach the audience directly. Whichever method you choose, distinguish what the audience hears from what other characters hear, and show how the information changes the next step.

heading.zh: 先保住内心描写的作用，再换载体
heading.en: Keep the thought’s function before changing its carrier

body.zh:
先问原文中的心理话是什么：**事实、人物推断、欲望，还是尚未决定的念头**？“她怀疑他来过”和“他确实来过”不能互换。再写一句功能说明：她因此相信什么、怕失去什么、打算隐瞒什么，或下一步怎样做。

| 原文作用 | 可选载体与边界 |
|---|---|
| 怀疑对方说谎 | 核对既有信息、改变问法；异常只支持怀疑，不自动确定责任人 |
| 想走又舍不得 | 拒绝催促、询问还能否联系；不必新增关键物件 |
| 不愿承认失败 | 改口、回避帮助、暂缓交出结果；保留原文真实结果 |
| 私人记忆影响选择 | 当前触发与回应、明确回忆或VO；现场人物不自动知道记忆内容 |

动作完全不变，并不证明心理句多余：它可能改变观众对同一动作的理解，或承担叙述风格。删改前比较人物行为与观众理解两方面。载体不必解释全部意义，但需要给出足以支持本场推断的依据。
body.en:
Identify what the original thought is: **fact, inference, desire, or an undecided possibility**. “She suspects he came here” cannot become “he came here.” Then state its function: what she believes, fears losing, intends to hide, or does next.

| Function | Possible carrier and limit |
|---|---|
| Suspects a lie | Check existing information or change the question; an anomaly does not identify its author |
| Wants to leave but hesitates | Resist a prompt or ask about future contact; no new key prop is required |
| Avoids admitting failure | Rephrase, refuse help, or delay handing over a result; keep the actual result |
| A private memory affects a choice | Present trigger and response, a marked memory, or VO; others do not automatically know its contents |

Unchanged action does not prove a thought is redundant: it may change the audience’s reading of that action or carry the chosen voice. Compare both behavior and audience understanding before cutting. The carrier need not explain every meaning, but it must support the inference this scene asks for.

heading.zh: 五种载体怎么选
heading.en: How to Choose Among Five Carriers

body.zh:
1. **行动后果**：人物做或不做一件有结果的事。
2. **证据反应**：他验证、藏起、退回或重新排列某项证据。
3. **空间动作**：靠近谁、挡住出口、换到另一方身边。
4. **关系对白**：把想法变成试探、拒绝、交换或质问，现场人物也会听见。
5. **主观声音**：只把必须明确而又不适合说出口的信息交给观众。

不要为每句心理活动配一个无功能微动作。倒水、看窗或攥手若没有改变议程与证据，只是把解释换成假运动。
body.en:
1. **Consequence of action:** The character does or declines something that produces a result.
2. **Response to evidence:** They verify, hide, return, or rearrange a piece of evidence.
3. **Spatial action:** They approach someone, block an exit, or move to the other person’s side.
4. **Relational dialogue:** The thought becomes a probe, refusal, exchange, or challenge that people in the scene can also hear.
5. **Subjective voice:** Give the audience only the private information that must be explicit but cannot naturally be spoken.

Do not assign a purposeless micro-gesture to every thought. Pouring water, looking out a window, or clenching a fist merely turns explanation into fake movement unless it changes the agenda, evidence, or choice.

heading.zh: VO、OS与对白：分清谁能听见
heading.en: VO, OS, and dialogue: identify who can hear

body.zh:
同一句“我不信他忘了密码”，作为对白会让听者知道自己被怀疑；作为本场明确的内心VO，只让观众知道；完全留白时，则由已有证据和人物行动支持观众推断。

Drama Skills 的格式中，**[VO]**用于非现场主观或叙述声音，**[OS]**用于同场景中未入画的说话者。例如门外同伴喊“车到了”是OS，人物仍能听见；“我现在还不能告诉她”若是内心声音，是VO，现场同伴不能据此接话。电话与录音要写清设备、实际播放和谁能听到，不能只因说话者没入画就当作内心。

VO可以增加画面无法独立给出的私人判断、隐瞒计划、跨时认知或有意反讽。画面已经明白演出的同一信息通常不必再念一遍；声音若改变意义或属于作品明确的风格，则按实际功能判断。已经接受节奏档案的项目按该项目的VO限制核对，没接受就不要替作者发明统一比例。
body.en:
“I don’t believe he forgot the password” alerts a listener to suspicion when spoken aloud. Marked as this character’s interior VO, it informs only the audience. Left unsaid, it needs existing evidence and action to support the audience’s inference.

In Drama Skills, **[VO]** identifies a nonlocal subjective or narrative voice; **[OS]** identifies an unseen speaker in the same scene. A companion outside calling “The car’s here” is OS and can be heard inside. An interior “I can’t tell her yet” is VO; the companion cannot reply to it. For a phone or recording, specify the device, actual playback, and listeners. An unseen speaker is not automatically an inner voice.

VO can add a private judgment, concealed plan, cross-time understanding, or deliberate irony unavailable from the picture alone. Avoid simply restating an already clear image, but judge changed meaning and deliberate style by function. Apply a VO limit from an accepted project pacing profile; do not invent a universal ratio for a project without one.

heading.zh: 原创范例：器材箱上的断封条
heading.en: Original example: the broken seal on an equipment case

body.zh:
虚构社区演出中，林澈负责在交接单上确认自己检查过的录音器材。器材员韩越保管储物室钥匙。前文已建立：林澈昨晚贴了完整的红封条，韩越今早说“今天没人开过箱”；其他值班人员也可能接触器材，封条破损的原因尚未查明。

待改的心理句是：“林澈怀疑韩越隐瞒了开箱情况，不想在还没检查时替整箱器材担保。”**不是**“韩越一定打开过，也一定拿走了东西”。

> 韩越把交接单和笔推到林澈面前。
>
> 林澈看见箱扣处的红封条断了。她把笔放回桌上，将箱子转向韩越。
>
> 林澈：昨晚贴的时候是整条。这个什么时候断的？
>
> 韩越：我没开。可能搬的时候刮到了。
>
> 林澈：那先一起点。我只签我看过的。
>
> 韩越取出保管的钥匙打开箱子。林澈拿起清单，韩越把清单上第一支话筒放到桌面，她核对型号和数量后，在对应条目旁作记号；整箱确认栏仍空着。

断封条让“不接受未经核对的交接”有依据，但不能唯一推出谁开过箱、何时开、有没有少物件。韩越解释也仍是说法，不是已验证的结论。打开箱子、核对第一项是实际动作；剩余项目未核对，就不要在场尾宣布整箱无误。

若必须把怀疑准确交给观众，可在看到断封条后加：**[VO] 林澈：他说今天没开过。我得先点清。**韩越不会听见这句。声音说出她在比较的事实与下一步意图，核对动作则真的执行这一步；后续若要确定责任，还需已有记录、证言或别的剧情依据。
body.en:
In a fictional community performance, Lin Che signs for recording equipment she has inspected. Equipment keeper Han Yue holds the storeroom key. Established facts: Lin Che applied an intact red seal last night; Han Yue said this morning that nobody opened the case today. Other staff could have handled it, and the damage is unexplained.

The thought to adapt is “Lin Che suspects Han Yue is withholding an opening of the case and refuses to certify equipment she has not checked.” It is **not** “Han Yue certainly opened it and took something.”

> Han Yue pushes the handover sheet and pen toward Lin Che.
>
> She sees the red seal broken at the latch. She returns the pen to the table and turns the case toward him.
>
> Lin Che: It was intact when I put it on last night. When did this break?
>
> Han Yue: I didn’t open it. It might have snagged while we moved it.
>
> Lin Che: Then let’s count together. I’ll sign for what I’ve checked.
>
> Han Yue uses the key he holds to open the case. Lin Che takes the list. He places the first listed microphone on the table; she checks its model and quantity and marks that item. The box for certifying the whole case remains blank.

The broken seal supports refusing an unchecked handover. It does not identify who opened the case, when, or whether anything is missing. Han Yue’s explanation is still a claim. Opening and checking one item actually occur; the scene cannot certify the remaining contents.

If the audience must know her suspicion precisely, add after the discovery: **[VO] Lin Che: He said nobody opened it today. I need to count first.** Han Yue cannot hear this. The voice gives her comparison and intent; the action executes the check. Establishing responsibility later requires records, testimony, or other story evidence.

heading.zh: 内心戏常见失败与修正
heading.en: Common Inner-Monologue Failures and Fixes

body.zh:
| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 动作段写“他意识到、她觉得” | 找到该认识改变的下一动作 |
| 每层心理都改成旁白 | 只保留必须直接给观众的私人信息 |
| 用攥拳、皱眉替代所有想法 | 让动作作用于证据、关系或选择 |
| 私人旁白说完，对手立刻接话 | 分清现场人物与观众的知情范围 |
| 完全留白，观众没有推断依据 | 提供一个能支持判断的行为或证据 |
| 旁白与画面重复同一事实 | 让声音增加画面无法独立给出的层次，或删掉 |
body.en:
| Failure | Fix |
|---|---|
| An action paragraph says “he realized” or “she felt” | Find the next action changed by that realization |
| Every layer of thought becomes voice-over | Keep only private information that must reach the audience directly |
| Clenched fists and frowns stand in for every thought | Make the action affect evidence, a relationship, or a choice |
| An opponent answers immediately after private voice-over | Separate what characters in the scene know from what the audience knows |
| Everything is left implicit, with no basis for inference | Supply one behavior or piece of evidence that supports the judgment |
| Voice-over repeats exactly what the image already shows | Let sound add a layer the image cannot provide, or remove it |

q.zh: 内心旁白是不是越少越好？
q.en: Should inner voice-over always be kept to a minimum?

a.zh: 没有统一多少。先看作品是否选择主观声音，以及信息能否由更有后果的行动承担。旁白能明确私人判断，但也会改变观众知情位置。
a.en: There is no universal amount. First consider whether the work uses a subjective voice and whether the information can be carried by an action with greater consequences. Voice-over can clarify private judgment, but it also changes the audience’s knowledge position.

q.zh: 人物沉默能表现心理吗？
q.en: Can silence express a character’s thoughts?

a.zh: 可以。沉默可让对方换策略，也可以让观众感到犹豫、距离、时间或气氛，不必每次都改变权力。先看它在本场承担什么，画面、声音与既有信息能否支持理解；只写停顿而没有可读作用时，再考虑压缩。
a.en: Yes. Silence may change another person’s tactic or communicate hesitation, distance, time, or atmosphere without shifting power each time. Judge its function and whether the picture, sound, and established information support it. Compress a pause when it has no readable purpose.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中用 /short-drama-write（Codex 中用 `$short-drama-write`）检查这段内心戏：先列心理信息改变的判断与选择，再比较行动、证据、空间、对白和主观声音载体；标清观众与现场人物分别知道什么，只改这一场，不扩写分镜。
text.en: In Claude Code, use `/short-drama-write` to inspect this inner-monologue passage. First list the judgments and choices changed by the psychological information, then compare action, evidence, space, dialogue, and subjective voice as carriers. Mark separately what the audience and the people in the scene know. Revise only this scene, without expanding it into a storyboard. In Codex, use `$short-drama-write`.
